Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules of varying sizes, some with ill-defined margins suggestive of necrosis or cavitation. In the context of chest pain and non-productive cough, this radiographic pattern is characteristic of Necrotizing Sarcoid Granulomatosis (NSG), a rare variant of sarcoidosis that presents with nodular opacities and vasculitis/granulomatous inflammation, distinguishing it from typical sarcoidosis (which usually shows hilar adenopathy) or metastatic cancer.
